entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vivek Kumar Birla,J.
Hon'ble Surendra Singh-I,J.
1. Heard Sri Virendra Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri A.N. Mulla,
learned A.G.A. for the State respondents.
2.

The present writ petition has been preferred with the prayer to quash the impugned First Information Report dated 29.04.2023, registered as Case Crime No. 0343 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 354, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act and Section 7/8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, P.S.Tajganj, District Agra and for a direction to the respondents not to arrest the petitioners in pursuance of impugned First Information Report.

entities.text: Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 1 3. At the very outset, learned AGA pointed out that Sections 7/8 of the POCSO Act have been deleted during investigation.

4. The submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that all alleged offences are punishable with imprisonment upto seven years, therefore the police authorities are bound to follow the procedure laid down under Section 41-A Cr.P.C.
The petitioners have been wrongly implicated and could not be arrested.

Reliance has been placed on the judgement of Apex Court in Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 273 and Social Action Forum for Manav Adhikar Vs. Union of India, Ministry of Law and Justice and others in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 73 of 2015 with Criminal Appeal No. 1265 of 2017, Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 156 of 2017, Satendra Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another, (2022) 10 SCC 51 and co-ordinate Division Bench of this Court in Vimal Kumar & 3 others Vs. State of U.P. & 3 others in 2021 (2) ACR 1147.

6. Accordingly, the instant petition also stands disposed of in terms of the judgements as noted above.
